Those who do not commit suicide and who are captured in the group are taken to Novi Kasaba to the soccer field where already some 3,000 people have been gathered, taken prisoners there of course. Now there is a prisoner who is in the hills, a prisoner, no, excuse me, a man who is trying to flee from the region. From the hills he saw a group with some 30 prisoners running up to the cross roads there at Janovici, that is right here. The men are lined up along the road facing three amoured vehicles, including one stolen UN APC. Once they are lined up the amoured vehicles open fire with their heavy machine gun and execute that group of 30 people. The BSA soldiers celebrate this event by letting out some screams, shooting up in the air. Some of them have their faces covered. There is a second group, again 30 people, the same thing happens. A third group also approaches. People are lined up and everyone is executed with this heavy machine gunfire and the witness left the scene at that point. Now another prisoner who had given the promises that were made via the loud speakers goes to the roadside. He is kept inside for a few hours, during which time other prisoners turn up and then he is put on a bus. The bus heads off towards the Jadar River, a place near the Drinjaca River in this area. He is in a group of 16. They are lined up along the river and once they are lined up soldiers open fire and execute all of the members of that group. Another group surrender en masse. They are kept along the side of the road before they are brought to the soccer field at Novi Kasaba, and on the way there a man who was trying to buy his freedom from one of the prisoners is killed by a gun shot through his head. Later in the afternoon a large number of prisoners who were there in the Novi Kasaba soccer field, that group was evacuated towards Kravica and Bratunac on trucks and buses. Now on the way they see a large group of prisoners which has just been captured or has surrendered, and there as well the prisoners have to hold up their three fingers, the Serbian victory sign. There is a witness among those prisoners. When they get to the road there is a person there in civilian clothes who climbs down from a vehicle and says that he will be taking over that group, that it will not be going to Kravica because at Kravica there is no more room to kill people. There is an amoured vehicle that approaches. Soldiers come down. They set up a machine gun facing the group of prisoners, but there is a convoy of refugees that is going by just at that moment. The civilian individual wants, once the convoy has gone by, starts hitting prisoners with an iron bar and the prisoners are directed to a field at Sandici, the same field where had been assembled those who were subsequently killed in the hangar. There they have to sing songs and later they will be evacuated towards Bratunac. While they are there in Sandici in that field, a woman is separated from the group of prisoners and she is gang raped by several soldiers right there in front of everyone. Then the soldiers discuss out loud how they are going to go about killing her. They mutilate her and they finish her off by cutting her throat.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have now prepared a film that I would like to show the court. Before showing that I would ask Mr. Ruez to please describe to the Court what they will be seeing on that film.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first scenes will show the evacuation of the refugees from Potocari. On the right in the picture there you will see a group of men, and I will point it out when the video is running, who are walking. They have not been mixed with anyone, that is to say, these are men who have been separated from the children, women and the elderly, and then they are directed towards Bratunac. The film then will show a few scenes from the roadside of prisoners, a prisoner who has to call on his countrymen to surrender, and then there are some anti-aircraft guns that are firing at the refugees who are trying to flee through the woods. We will also see the surrender of prisoners. There is a BSA soldier wearing a blue helmet near Kravica, so you will see him on the video as well. Then to finish there will be some scenes of the arrival of refugees in Kladanj and then there will be some scenes of the arrival of BSA soldiers in Bosnian territory after a few days of confrontation in the woods. There was a battle there around Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Would you please lower the lights and play Exhibit 3 clip 2. (Exhibit 3 Clip 2 was played).

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A UN compound at Potocari, a Dutch battalion. On the way you can see the buses there waiting in a row. Men walking on the left-hand side of the road. Between the trucks the soldiers who see to it that the men cannot cross over and mix with the other people. Women, children the elderly walking on the right-hand side. There are a few men there, but that does not mean they will be able to get to on any buses because the separation process is an ongoing one. This is the separation line before going to the buses. The Dutch Battalion had set up some vehicles there to try to straighten things out a little bit before people got on to the buses. The evacuation process is just about over. This is on 13th. This is when this has been filmed. These are things that have been left by people before boarding the buses. This is a soldier who has been forced to call on the other soldiers to surrender. "Come, surrender to the Serbs", the other one yells. These are soldiers who are guarding prisoners. They are sitting down in a field nearby. The person who made this film cut off the filming because there was something happening there in the field no doubt. There is a group of prisoners there that has been gathered together. This is a 30 millimetre anti-aircraft gunfire against people trying to flee through the woods. This is a very devastating weapon, anti-personnel use. Along the road, this is a strategic road, Bratunac/Nova Kasaba, there you see there are soldiers set up every 30 metres. Here you can see the hills through which the refugees tried to flee. Now this is Kravica, the Kravica region. That was one of the main areas where a lot of prisoners surrendered. You will see some men on the top of the hill here, and they are going to go down towards the road to surrender. There the soldiers are counting them. There is a blue helmet being worn by a BSA soldier. You can see the bags there left by those who surrendered previously. These are prisoners arriving. A man who as has been forced to give an interview to the camera man is asking him how many days he has been in the woods. He says, "How is it you look like you are frightened?" and the man says, "Who wouldn't be frightened?" A soldier amongst the civilians who has to take off his army t-shirt. These are buses and trucks waiting to take the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could we have the lights again, please? Mr. Ruez, on the film that we have just seen we can see full face a number of Bosnian Muslim men who were surrendered to the Bosnian Serb Army. What have you done in order to attempt to identify those persons shown in the film?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What we have done is we have prepared still photos using all the material we had available, and those photos were sent to the Bosnian Ministry of the Interior so that there could be an identification process launched so we could identify as many people as possible. By way of example, I would like to show you a few ----

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Ruez is now going to refer to Exhibits 8 through 22 that are in your binders. Mr. Ruez would you please show some of those photographs? Could we dim the lights please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This picture, for instance, was made from a video where men had been filmed at Potocari.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Just one question, Mr. Harmon. What is the source of that video?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The source of the video, that is from a Serbian journalist. Sometimes he says he is from Independent Serbian TV; sometimes he says he works for the police. It depends on the situation. It changes. This picture is from the video. This is a man who is walking on the left-hand side of the road next to the trucks. This is a picture of a man who is forced to call out to the refugees in the woods to come and surrender to the Serbians who were along the road. A picture of the man who gave that very brief interview to the journalist who was filming the process while the prisoners were surrendering. Here again several recognisable faces among the men who were giving up surrendering. This was in Sandici, the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much, Mr. Ruez. Your Honours, we will be presenting evidence later in this hearing about the results of those investigations. Mr. Ruez, you have mentioned in your testimony on a number of occasions that UN blue helmets and UN blue flat jackets and other equipment were routinely stolen by Bosnian Serb soldiers during the course of the takeover in Srebrenica. While you were in the Bosnia conducting your investigations in this case did you recover any stolen UN helmets and flat jackets?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could you please explain the circumstances of the recovery?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 4th June we did a search of a container which was in front of staff headquarters in Bratunac. Inside the container among the various types of military equipment that we found there were 28 blue helmets and 11 bulletproof vests. The blue helmets had been repainted a blue-ish grey. Cyrillic names were written on the helmets, but there were also Dutch indications inside, and on the bulletproof vests there were labels written in Dutch with the instructions inside the vests as well as a few names.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Has the Office of the Prosecutor contacted Dutch soldiers by those names that were found inside the vests and inside the helmets?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The soldiers who were able to be identified as being the owners of the equipment were questioned. All of the objects discovered had been stolen under various circumstances, but mostly as concerns this group it was during the point that their observation point was captured and they were being kept as hostages.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Where were the Muslim prisoners who had been captured or surrendered taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those that were not immediately executed when they were arrested or at the point they were gathering together, were put on to buses and trucks. Some of them did not have any means of transportation. On the evening of 13th we do know that orders had been given to execute some of the prisoners who remained in the fields and who could no longer be transported. Those who were transported had as the main destination the city of Bratunac. They were taken into the former school of Bratunac which is behind the Vuk Karadzic School. There they remained inside the school where they went through a process that went on all night long. Soldiers came in. They were wearing military camouflage outfits. There were poljica inscriptions on the sleeves of their jackets. On the screen I think some things are going on? OK. When those who were in the school were put into classrooms immediately some of them began to be beaten, beaten by the military police. They were beaten with rifle butts on their heads very brutally. Other prisoners arrived while that was going on. The prisoners were then taken outside, at least some of them were. Those inside did not know what was going on outside. They could hear screams of pain, shots, noises and assumed that those who had been taken out were or had been executed since they did not see them come back. Other groups of prisoners remained on the buses and trucks. A column was stationed in front of the Vihor Company which is a local Bratunac transportation company. Throughout the night soldiers asked the men who were in the trucks questions. Asked them, for example, those who came from certain villages to identify themselves. People did not know what was the reason for the questions. They answered. Others did not dare to answer or others did answer because they were afraid not to, knowing that they would be executed if they came from a place where they were not supposed to come from. Those who got off of the trucks were beaten. People heard shots there as well and people got back on the buses. The same situation took place with a group of prisoners who had spent the night on buses in front of the Vuk Karadzic School. Men were separated from others. Some were beaten. People heard shots. A witness saw a member of the Military Police who killed a mentally retarded person, saying that this person had brushed against his bulletproof vest. Others said, no, that is not something that should be done, that is, they should not brush against his vest. Then he said "Kill him" and he did that with a burst of his machine gun. Others remained inside the buses and trucks, not in Bratunac but in Kravica, between Bratunac and Kravica, and no specific event was mentioned by that group. Prisoners were already in Bratunac at that point. Those who had been separated on 12th in the afternoon had already been taken to Bratunac, and they were then at that point in a hangar. They were also experiencing the same process, separation of certain men who were taken outside. Noises of firing was heard and the group was evacuated during the night, put on to buses and trucks and then transported to the north to a little hamlet which is called Lazete where they were placed into a gymnasium of the school in Grbavci. The school is on the map right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, you also mentioned that some men had arrived in the village of Tisca. Can you explain what happened to those men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those who had been separated from the other bus passengers and those on the trucks and, therefore, put into the teachers' school, spent the afternoon waiting there. In the evening soldiers came, began beating the prisoners. The beating went on for several hours until 1 o'clock and then at 1 o'clock in the morning a truck arrived. The prisoners were put on to the truck. They were transported near Vlasenica. Before they arrived there the truck moved in the direction of the woods. After having turned one of the prisoners escaped from the truck right before it stopped. He was able to see that those who were on the truck arrived in a field where there were already bodies. As he was fleeing he could hear automatic fire coming from the direction where the bus had stopped, where the truck had stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I would like to turn your attention to 14th July and I would like to ask you what happened to the Muslim prisoners who were being detained in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The prisoners who were in Bratunac spent the night under the conditions I have already described. Those who were in the former school remained there throughout the day. The process continued throughout the day. In the same way, people were taken out. Some were taken out of the classrooms, taken outside. There were cries, screams, firing heard and others were evacuated. The convoys went towards Lazete and also took other prisoners to the school at Grbavci which is about 50 kilometres north of Bratunac. The last convoys of the day no longer took them to that same point, but further north near Pilica about 60 kilometres north of Bratunac where they were also put into schools or rather into a school.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What happened to the prisoners who were taken to Grbavci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those who had been there since the preceding night spent the night in a gymnasium. Nothing specific took place during the night, except for the fact that prisoners did not have very much to drink. They were suffering terribly from the heat. They were piled one on top of the other. They could not go to the toilet. At the beginning of the afternoon those who were in the gymnasium were taken out in small groups of 30 to do so. They had to go through a kind of an opening which was the entrance point to the gymnasium. They were given a glass of water by the soldiers and each of the prisoners was blindfolded with a piece of a t-shirt. They were put on a truck and taken to a field which was about 1 kilometre from the school. When they got off the trucks the men were set up in rows and immediately after that fire was opened. All those prisoners who had been taken were executed. Others arrived in the afternoon at that school. There was no longer any room in the gymnasium which was being evacuated, and the prisoners were put inside the school in classrooms. They were not allowed to get up. If anybody did the soldier outside would fire through the windows and try to hit the person who was inside the classroom. Some people there were hit, wounded, and then for that group as well the transportation began. The prisoners had their hands tied behind their backs. They were led to another execution site which is about 5 to 10 kilometres away near a lake. They were not blindfolded. There were already piles of bodies there when they arrived. The soldiers were drunk. They were joking about the prisoners. They were telling them to choose a free place, an open spot, among the bodies. As soon as there were enough of the prisoners there the soldiers all around opened fire and also executed those prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, do you have any estimates of how many prisoners were executed? I am speaking specifically of the prisoners who had been held in the gym and in the school at Grbavci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On that day the number who were executed, well, since the estimates that were made by various witnesses fluctuate, several hundred, there is no doubt about that, in so far as the ability -- there was storage space for that many at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, would this be an appropriate time to break?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harmon. The hearing will resume at 2.30. The court stands adjourned.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The court is in session again. Would you please be seated? Mr. Harmon, the witness can be brought in again.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, your Honour. MR. JEAN RENE RUEZ, recalled

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We can resume. Mr. Harmon, I give you the floor to continue the questions you want to ask your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Examined by MR. HARMON, continued

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, when we broke before lunch you were testifying about what happened to prisoners that had been left in Grbavci. I would like to keep you along the same line of questioning. We are on 14th July. I would like to ask you what happened to the prisoners who had been transported north of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is not understood by the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me ask that question again. What happened to the prisoners who had been transported north of Zvornik on 14th July?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the executions which took place in the Grbavci school on 14th July, those people who were in the school, that is, in the Pilica regional school, experienced the same fate that they had had when they were in the old school in Bratunac. Some of the people were taken out by the Bosnian Serb soldiers. There were screams heard, there were shots heard and those people did not come back to the prisoners who were inside the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Will you slow down just a little bit in your answers? Thank you. What happened to the survivors who remained in the woods on 14th July?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the woods, things remained more or less the same. They continue to be hunted. The troop of refugees was trying to find a way to find a strategic road leading to Nova Kasaba. Some of them succeeded in doing so; others were taken prisoner. A witness who was on a hill overlooking the area, specifically the intersection at Konjevici, saw three buses painted white, filled with people, that turned on to a small road leading towards Cerska in the hills, into a valley. The three buses were followed by an armoured vehicle. Shortly after that vehicle passed by an excavator followed the column. There was heavy firing heard from the direction that the buses had taken. Immediately afterwards, they were seen going back towards Konjevic Polje as well as the armoured vehicle. The excavator reappeared 30 minutes later. The fate of those prisoners at that point, the prisoners in the buses, were not yet known; but in the evening some witnesses were able to get through that area and in the morning along the road rising to Cerska they saw a row of bodies lined up in the grass along the edge of the road. They were frightened and they fled.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, I would like now to turn your attention to July 15th and ask you to continue your testimony about the fate of the people who were in the woods.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Many were arrested, many surrendered. Most of them were concentrated in the soccer field, the Nova Kasaba soccer field. There were people who were looking around to find what would be the best moment in order to cross over the line. They saw that those soldiers who were guarding the groups of prisoners took away 15 to 20 people in a group at a time toward the Jadar River and from that point you could hear shots being fired.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: When you say the name of a place, would you point it out, please, on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The episode I have just spoken about took place here. The episode that we are speaking about now in the Novi Kasaba soccer field was here. The group of prisoners which was in the Nova Kasaba soccer field, that is, those who were not taken away in small groups towards the river, were seen being evacuated at the end of the day in a few buses. Most of them followed the buses in a column on foot, but we do not know what happened to them. Between Nova Kasaba and the Konjevici intersection which is here, witnesses in the hills noted that in small groups individuals were surrendering on the road, going down to the road to surrender. Their fate was immediate. Those who had a weapon with them were given a shovel, forced to dig a hole and were immediately executed when they fell into the hole. Those who did not have shovels were also executed, that is, those who did not have any arms, did not have to dig their own graves but were executed anyway a little bit further on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The executioners, were they members of the Bosnian Serb Army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These were soldiers who were wearing camouflage uniforms of the Bosnian Serb Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: On 15th July, Mr. Ruez, were there prisoners still being detained in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a last group of prisoners were still in Bratunac on 15th July. Around noon the prisoners who were in the old school were loaded on to seven buses. They were taken to the north of Zvornik, to a school, and in the school the process which I have already described took place again. Some of them were beaten, others were taken out and shots were again heard. A prisoner who went to look for water for his fellow detainees noted the arrival of a bus in the evening. On the bus was a group of prisoners. The group was not taken to the school, but instead was taken to a field near the school. Again shots were heard from that field.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Would you kindly point on the map to your left where that school was located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The school is about 60 kilometres north of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, I would now like to turn your attention to July 16th and ask you what happened to those prisoners who were in the school in Grbavci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During the morning of 16th July, according to the testimonies of the survivors, the Bosnian Serb soldiers spoke to the prisoners and told them that they would be exchanged. They had their hands tied behind their backs. They were loaded on to buses. They were not allowed to look at what was going on around them. They were taken over a very short distance toward a field. Once they arrived at the field, the buses remained one behind the other. Those people who were inside the buses were taken out in groups. When they were able to look around them, they saw that there were some bodies already stretched out on the ground. They then heard shots. Their turn finally came. They were led into the field, lined up and executed immediately. Once the execution had taken place the buses left, and then subsequently came back with other groups of prisoners. These facts about the executions that day were indicated in a -- they were confirmed by a Bosnian Serb soldier who was on the spot when that happened. I have interviewed him and he recognised what happened and gave a similar description to that of the witnesses and Erdemovic, in fact, has pleaded guilty before this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Approximately, how many prisoners were killed on that site on 16th July?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to the estimates of Drazan Erdemovic, approximately 1200 people were executed at that site.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, now I would like to focus your attention on the events that occurred after 16th July. If you could briefly summarise some of the other incidents where there were mass executions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The situation in the forests continued as it had. A group of refugees continued to try to find a way out, a way out of the situation in which they found themselves. Some of them noted what was going on. 150 prisoners were seen being arrested or in Konjevici; most of them were immediately executed and the others were taken into an area, to an area that no-one knows. In the area of Udric, which is on the escape route of the refugees column, a witness observed that a group of 150 people approximately were surrendering to the Bosnian Serb soldiers. The group was immediately shot. The next morning a group of 250 people was captured. In the morning an excavator appeared on site, dug a hole. The prisoners were ordered to gather around the hole. The soldiers surrounded them, the excavator pushed the people into the hole and ordered to bury them. Those who tried to escape were immediately shot by these soldiers surrounding the group of prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, do you have any estimates on how many people are missing from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are several figures that have been put forth. The highest estimate which was one from the civilian authorities gives a figure of missing at about 10,300 people, but this estimate has not yet been totally confirmed. It should also be pointed out that the process of prisoner exchange, according to the Dayton Agreement, has been concluded now for approximately three months.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, have you and other investigators from the Office of the Prosecutor travelled to Bosnia and Herzegovina and conducted preliminary investigations of execution sites and mass grave sites?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the first missions on site were taken -- took place on 21st January of this year and there were other trips that took place since then.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Have your preliminary findings at those sites confirmed executions that are associated with the testimonies of witnesses that you have received?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me take you through a series of those sites, if I can. Did you visit a grave site in Cerska? When you are answering that, if you would please point on the map the location so the court can see exactly where it is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the light of the explanations that some witnesses gave about the situation, one site was analysed. It is halfway to Cerska, about three kilometres from the asphalt road where the three white buses were seen taking the potential prisoners and where heavy firing was heard by witnesses, where the lined up corpses were seen, as well as an area which might be a mass grave was identified by other witnesses who went through that area a month after what had happened. When they were going backwards, since they could not go across the confrontation line, they decided they would go in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I would like to show you Exhibits 23 through to 27 and ask you to identify those exhibits. I would ask you to show them on the elmo and describe to the court what each of those exhibits represents. If we could have the lights dimmed, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This photograph which was taken at the end of May of this year shows the earth road which leads from the asphalt road which goes into Cerska Valley, in the direction of Cerska. This area which is on the left part of the photograph shows that a great amount of earth was removed from this hill on the left. The right side of the road is covered with earth over which a lot of branches were put down which would make people think that logging had been going on there. Three holes were dug along this road in order to ascertain whether there were bodies buried at that place. The three holes are where you see my colleagues dressed in blue who were in the process of digging. In the first of those holes a human body appears. One can see the hip over here, wearing civilian clothing, a jacket, and here is the skull. There is a round hole which appears there at the bottom of the skull. The second hole one can see legs, actually three legs; two which belong to the same person and another leg wearing a different shoe from the ones you see on the other two legs and, therefore, belong to another person. The third hole shows us a human, a human skull. One can still see the hair on the scalp. This round piece is missing at the top of the skull.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, do you have something else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Along the road a search was conducted in order to look for shells. It was not possible to go through the entire area because there was not enough time and given environmental conditions, but along about 10 metres there were about 60 different cases that were found.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you also visit grave sites near Nova Kasaba?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could we please have the lights dimmed again? Mr. Ruez, I am going to show you Exhibits Nos. 28 and 29. I would ask you to please explain to the court what they depict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is an aerial photograph which was taken on 27th July 1995. One can see the road on the photograph. It should be in -- you should have a clear picture of it. Here is the road. These two squares are houses, completely destroyed. The roof has gone and on this photo one can see an area of earth which has been moved about, and it is very clear and it was moved about very recently, as well as traces of vehicles approaching the area. This is another aerial photograph taken on the same date right next to the first photograph. Two other areas of freshly moved earth can be very easily seen here and here. Our research was really directed on that site.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What killings are these sites associated with, Mr. Ruez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The photographed area is right next to the Nova Kasaba football field. According to testimonies that were taken, a certain number of prisoners were executed right near there, right near that stadium. Another solution might be that those who were fighting had crossed over this area, and bodies might be the result of fighting that might have taken place at that point. That is what our research tried to ascertain.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could you please refer to Exhibits 30 through 35 and explain what they depict? Could we have the lights dimmed once again, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the area that I showed you on the aerial photograph, we dug a three-metre hole by two metres which was about 80 centimetres deep. There you can see the first layer of people. The first layer shows six bodies. This is the first body. Under it is a second one, another one, another one and another one. Another part of a body can be seen here. On this body which is clearly visible one can see that the person was wearing civilian clothes. He is wearing a civilian shirt. This body, we see the back, the back here and the head there. We can see that the hands, the arms, have been tied behind the back with a small rope and then in the next photograph -----

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Would you stop there for a second? Mr. Cleaver, can you focus down on the -----

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: OK, that is fine.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This photograph clearly shows that person's hands tied behind his back with a small rope, a small cord, which might have actually have been a shoe lace. Here is the hand. This man is also wearing civilian clothes. He was wearing a bright blue, blue, green, white jacket. His hands are also tied behind his back, actually lying on the head of the person under him. In the next picture we will see that more clearly. In this photo we can see that the person's hands were tied with iron wire which is here. Here are the person's hands with the fingers and here is his wedding ring which you can see here. For the people who were discovered in the mass grave were all wearing civilians clothes, at least those we could see. Two of them whose arms we could see, we could see that the arms were tied behind their backs.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, would you point out to Nova Kasaba on the map which is to your left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nova Kasaba is found here. It is located here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you next visit a site Tatar Glogova? Would you please point that out on the map as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Tatar Glogova site is here and it is near Kravica which was just recently mentioned. The site is actually here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me refer you to Exhibits 36 and 37 and ask you to inform the court what they depict. Could we have the lights dimmed once again, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is an aerial photo of 7th July 1995. It shows you the road going from Kravica to Bratunac. This is a secondary road inside the old village which was also destroyed. A bulldozer can be seen here at the intersection. These two lighter coloured zones, this one and that one let you think that some event took place here and there because the ground was fresh and freshly dug up.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, let me ask you, based on your preliminary field work at that particular location, did you form an opinion as to whether there had been bodies at those particular sites?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: OK. Let me refer you to Exhibits 38 to 42. Please would you explain to the court what those exhibits represent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This photo was taken on the ground. It was the freshly moved ground of which you had an aerial view, so you can see heavy equipment was used in digging this soil. On the site we found several bones, for example, a long bone, a femur. Here you can see the femur. On the second site we also found bones. Here is a long bone next to a shoe. This is a close up of the shoe with the bone next to it. Also close by another example of human bones. This is a piece of a jaw bone.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In your opinion, Mr. Ruez, had these sites that you inspected been tampered with before you had the opportunity to inspect them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is quite probable, bearing in mind the human remains we saw, that the bodies might have been found at that spot. The information which we got from our aerial images confirms that view.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me show you Exhibits 43 and 44 and ask them to be displayed and would you please explain those images to the court? Could we have the lights dimmed once again, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So on this image you have two photos, one of 27th July 1995, which shows you a site, a possible burial site, and the second of 20th October 1995 which shows much activity which took place during that day. There is a hole there which you can see which has been done by the excavator which you can see there. Bearing in mind the human debris we found, it is possible to imagine that the bodies were buried here, but then taken away and some of the debris remained behind. This photo which was taken on 30th October upholds that hypothesis. After the first site was disturbed, a front loader was active at a second site.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, did you, in addition to those sites you have described, visit a grave site at some rail road tracks near Lazete?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you point on the map behind you where Lazete is located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Lazete is slightly north of Zvornik, here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What killings is that particular site associated with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This site was the one where prisoners were taken who were in the Grbavci school and who were executed on 14th July. It started at the beginning of the afternoon at about 2 o'clock and continued throughout the afternoon until the evening until about 23 o'clock. Heavy equipment was seen on the site by people who witnessed the execution taking place.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me show you Exhibit No. 45 and ask you to describe what it depicts. Could we have the lights dimmed again, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Based on the indications given to us by some survivors of the site, we had material, photographic material, which we could use. These photos show here are the railway tracks, here we have a road. This road goes towards the school of Grbavci which is about one kilometre away. The field here has no suspect traces of anything, but the field here also does not have any suspected sites. This goes back to the 22 July. The prisoners who say they were executed in the beginning in this part of the site, their statements are corroborated by activities which we saw here which is clearly visible on 22nd July. This site of execution, once it was strewn with bodies, was changed and then executions continued in another field later on. So they had to cross the railway tracks and all this part of the field shows significant traces of freshly moved or dug out soil.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Would you please refer to Exhibits 46 through 48 and describe your preliminary findings to the court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This photograph shows you the site which was used in the beginning. Here was the execution area. It is supposed to be here, and this is the zone where the aerial photo was taken where we could see that the soil had been dug out. We could not really go into detailed analysis because there was a lot of water when we were carrying out our investigations, so we concentrated on the second site. At the second site we found some human remains, pieces of bone, a complete skeleton. We dug a hole and we saw some bodies that were very strongly decomposing. The soil was mixed with human remains. There were also some bullets which we found on the site. That shows the characteristics that you have fresh traces which shows that the soil was moved or dug out in that area. On two occasions you have wheel tracks, old wheel tracks, which are covered up by fresher tracks. This photo shows a skeleton or at least a part of a skeleton. Here you see the spinal cord.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In your opinion, Mr. Ruez, had this site also been disturbed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am sure of it. At the site itself there are major changes when you compare the old and new disturbances. The fact that the site was dug up afterwards as well, this has been confirmed by a journalist who went to the spot before, one could have a guaranteed access to the area, upholds the fact that this site was disturbed after the date of executions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, did you and other investigators visit a grave site at a dam near Lazete?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Would you describe to the court what that particular site is associated with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 14th July, execution of prisoners took place at the Grbavci school. That took place at two sites. The first site was the one I have just outlined to you. For those who went to the school during the afternoon, or at the beginning of the evening, the execution site was the top of the dam around a lake which is found just to the north of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me show you Exhibit No. 49 and ask you to tell the court what this particular image depicts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On this photo you can see here the dam. This is a plateau which is at the dam. This is a slope which goes downwards to the soil over here, so this is the site where the executions took place. This photo was taken on 5th July and has no special characteristic. The photo taken on 27th July shows that on this part here you can see activity has been taking place, heavy machinery was used. There are signs of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Would you please refer to Exhibits 50 and 51 and please use them when you explain the results of your preliminary findings at that particular site?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a photo that shows the plateau which I have just mentioned. On this plateau executions are reported to have taken place. We saw and collected several bones that were strewn on the ground. We also saw -- we also collected bullets that we found on the site, over 1,000, 1,030. The part here is a possible mass grave. According to the statements of survivors, the bodies were later loaded on to a truck. So we cannot exclude the possibility of a mass grave in this part here because the soil here was heavily disturbed, and many of the bones we discovered were found in this area. The executions took place over the entire plateau. The cartridges we found were found over the entire area. A more specific area where there were many cartridges is here. Many pieces of skull were found in this area as well. Here is an example of the bones we found at the part where the soil was heavily disturbed. All these bones come from human beings. There is a bit of the skull, the spine, different bones, the ribs.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In your opinion, Mr. Ruez, had this site also been disturbed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is difficult to say. To the extent, as I have explained, that many of the bodies of the executed people were transported by truck to an unknown destination. These bones could perhaps come from individuals who were left behind or, indeed, it could be that they dug up the area and removed the human remains.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: OK.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is too early to make any special statement on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I would like to turn to your preliminary site investigations of the Branjevo farm near Pilica. Could you first turn to the map to your left, Mr. Ruez, and point out that particular site?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Pilica site is to the most northern part of the area we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Approximately, how many kilometres is that from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a little more than 60 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, what is that particular site associated with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That site is where executions took place by Drazen Erdemovic and it was also described to us by survivors.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Would you please now refer to Exhibits 52 and 53 and let me ask you to explain what they depict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These are two aerial photos. The first of 5th July 1995. This shows you the farm which is here in this area. The fields here and also here, and a wooded area. No particular activity was noticed in these two areas. On the photo of 17th July 1995, the day after the execution as described and the day when the survivors were managed to flee from the massacre which took place here. Machine activity is clearly visible at this part here, and here we saw some bodies. The enlargement of this part will be seen on the next photograph. This photo shows some of the bodies which are the points, the dots you can see here. The execution zone continues over this entire part. These points here represent bodies as well. A group of bodies was also found here near the zone where the soil had been dug out.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: On how many occasions did you and other investigators visit this particular site?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first time when we went there was when we were carrying out investigations was on 20th March this year. I went there again on 22nd March, when an officer visited and then we also went back there in the beginning of July this year.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Using Exhibits 54 through 56, can you explain to the court your findings at that particular site?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first elements which we saw when we came to the execution zone was the presence of shoes. There were several shoes at that site, either just on top of the soil or slightly buried by the soil. This is a tennis shoe, for example which was pointed into the soil. On the site itself we saw several bones. On this photo, for example, you can see a bit of a hip, of a rib. An entire part of the body can be seen here which is in the immediate vicinity of the area which had heavily disturbed soil on the aerial photo. Here you can see the part of the body. Some pieces of flesh were still attached to the bones of the body.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: As a result of your three visits to those sites, did you form an opinion as to whether that particular site had been disturbed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since 20th March, no activity has taken place on that site. However, according to information we have, this site was subject, as we mentioned before, it was subject to an attempt to be destroyed or disturbed. The next photos will help me explain the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Would you then refer to the next photos which are Exhibits 57 and 58, please? What is the date that particular image was taken, Mr. Ruez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This photo, 21st September 1995, and it shows once again on 21st September activities which took place on the very site itself where the mass grave was previously identified. This photograph of 27th September shows you the activity which is still taking place; you can see evidence of machinery being used. There is a deep hole that has been dug here, and inside the building of the farm you have an excavator and a hoe. We carried out investigations here and we found some cartridges. The field was also heavily investigated. About 60 cartridge shells were found on the surface of the soil. This corresponds to the area where the executions allegedly took place which we saw from the aerial image.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. If we could have the lights back on now? Now I will turn, Mr. Ruez, your attention to a map that is underneath the large white map that is on the board to your left. Your Honour, we just need to take a minute to remove that particular map to get to the map that is underneath it. Is that map in a good location to get the video monitor on it? I am not sure it is showing up on the video screen. Perhaps it has to be repositioned. Your Honour, perhaps we could take a brief break at this moment so we can get the correct camera angle on this map?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, I think that that is a very welcome suggestion. We will straighten out the map. So shall we have a recess or should we just wait to do it in the next few minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I leave it to the court's discretion.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We are going to step out for a few minutes so that the map can be set up, so that both the Judges and the public will be able to follow what the witness has to say. So we are going to have a recess for a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honours. (To the witness): Mr. Ruez, I am going to ask you some questions to explain what is on that map. Can we have a pan on that map, please? Mr. Ruez -- OK.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now, on this map you can see that we have different colours here. In fact, green, these are the areas there was a concentration of prisoner sites; in red, you have the mass graves and the blue is the mass graves that have been identified in connection with our investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Would you please just take each of those sites in order, Mr. Ruez, and explain what that map depicts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first site is in the south. This is a city of Srebrenica where, according to a witness, the people remaining there were gathered at the football soccer stadium. There were individual executions and with regard to the people gathered there, we do not know what became of them. At Potocari, there were 25,000 refugees who were gathered there. There were a large number of executions. That is the red. Bratunac, this was mainly a transit centre for prisoners because the first prisoners got there on the 12th. Men were separated from the other refugees at Potocari. In the course of the 13th, then people gathered along the strategic road and in the evening they were led to Bratunac where they were put in the old school, in the convoys of buses and trucks that remained before the Vihor bus company and at the school, and then also between Kravica and Bratunac. That is the last group that was held in a hangar there. Now, when the column was fleeing from the Srebrenica enclave going this way, the main ambush of Kamenica took place here. A lot of prisoners in the hours thereafter and in the following day were brought together in a field that was used for several groups on several occasions at Sandici. Some of those prisoners, at least, were transferred to Kravica, placed in the hangar where they were all executed. The two mass graves that are nearby, Tatar Glogova, and the sites have probably been moved. Here, where it was impossible for the refugees to flee towards Tuzla, there are several executions sites that have been indicated, mainly at the Konjevici intersection, and also in the whole area along the strategic road between Konjevic Polji and Nova Kasaba. Now, at Nova Kasaba a large number of prisoners were gathered as of 13th and the site was used as a point for a concentration of prisoners in the following days. A number of executions had been reported along the Jadar River. Now, three potential mass graves exist here, right near the soccer field. One of them has been analysed, and you saw that in the pictures which I showed you earlier on. In Cerska Valley, groups were taken there and executed and a mass grave is on the site of execution. On the road towards Kladanj, prisoners, males were separated from the buses, put in the school at Tisca, taken by truck to the hills near Vlasenica and executed. Prisoners who were gathered at Bratunac were convoyed by truck first in the night of 12th to 13th along the road that follows the border with Serbia towards Zvornik, Lazete, the school Grbavci. From there they were taken in the course of the day, the 14th, to an execution site nearby near Lazete. Two mass graves are there. At least one of them was probably tampered with the bodies or, at least, some of the bodies have been removed in the meantime. The prisoners there, for those who arrived in the afternoon of 14th and in the evening, those prisoners were transported by truck to the plateau of the dam -- that is up here -- where they were executed. There is a potential mass grave there, but we still have to check up on that. The prisoners were taken, some of them on 13th, others were taken on 15th, in the direction of the school, Pilica. This is the greatest distance to the north. So, first, they were about to gather in that school. Some of them remained there two days, two nights. Finally, they were taken to the Branjevo farm where they were executed. A mass grave was there at the site of execution. Some of the bodies have probably been moved in the meantime. There is something that is worth mentioning with regard to this map. The road followed the path followed by the column to flee, so you can see that there is quite a bit of fair ground covered in that. It is quite distant from the execution sites there to the north of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, was General Mladic seen at any of these locations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, General Mladic was seen at several of these sites.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Would you please mark on the map the particular locations where he was seen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For practical reasons I am going to have to put some labels, some stickers, black -- these black stickers will indicate where Mladic went to over those several days. The first site where Mladic was seen was at Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So at Srebrenica, we saw the video clip earlier on and we already know what General Mladic had to say on that occasion. The second site is at Potocari.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And Mladic was there the following day, that is to say, July 12th. He had a little bit of a conference with the journalist, talked to the crowd, but he was also seen visiting the men who had separated from the other refugees and put in the houses awaiting transfer towards Bratunac, and he tells them that they are going to be exchanged subsequently. Now, still the 12th, General Mladic was seen at Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He visits the detainees who were being held in a hangar at Bratunac, and he tells them as well that they will subsequently be exchanged. Now, in the night from 12th to 13th those prisoners were evacuated towards the school at Grbavci and General Mladic is seen at the time that they are evacuated to go to that school at Grbavci. In the course of 13th -- (The witness placed a label on the map) -- General Mladic goes to the field where a lot of prisoners are concentrated at Sandici and the prisoners have been there for five hours. One prisoner was killed there. He made some -- rather, he showed up afterwards. He talks to the prisoners and he tells them again that they will be exchanged. 15 minutes after General Mladic leaves, all of these prisoners are taken and taken in a hangar at Kravica where they are all executed. That same day, on the 13th, that is, General Mladic was seen speaking to a crowd of prisoners before they were transferred to the Nova Kasaba football stadium.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And he tells the crowd there they will be exchanged later on as well. He participates personally in the separation of a group of some 30 men from these prisoners without telling them why they are being separated from the others. Then he goes to Nova Kasaba -- (The witness placed a label on the map) -- to the soccer field and there again he speaks to the crowd. He usually starts by saying the same thing, "Hello, neighbours. Do you know who I am? I am General Mladic". Then he makes a number of comments about the situation and usually concludes by saying that the prisoners will be exchanged later on. The following day, 14th July, General Mladic is seen at the Grbavci school.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He speaks to the prisoners. He explains to them that there are some technical difficulties involved in their exchange, but that the situation should be improving and shortly after his departure the prisoners are given a glass of water, are blindfolded and are taken to the execution site nearby. In the evening, General Mladic was seen at that execution site while the executions are taking place.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ruez. Now let me change the subject and ask you since the takeover of Srebrenica has Dr. Karadzic or representatives of the Republika Srpska made public statements about the events that occurred in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could you please inform the court what they said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The comments of General Mladic are few and far between. The explanation that seems to be given as regards the existence of these mass graves in the area amounts, basically, to saying that the bodies in those graves are those of soldiers who were killed in the course of combat, and who were then buried for reasons of hygiene. Radovan Karadzic, for his part, made a few comments to the press. On 17th July 1995 he was speaking to television, Banja Luka Serbian television, and I am going to read this in English, if you do not mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I do not mind.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "In the past several days, the international media aided by the Muslim authorities have used vile propaganda unrealistically reporting on the events relating to a situation in Srebrenica. The accusation concerning alleged torture, killing, rape and deportation of Muslim civilians are being repeated without any independent verification. The truth is that none of these accusations have a firm basis".

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, this, for the record, is a press release issued by Jovan Zametica who was an adviser to Radovan Karadzic. (To the witness): Please continue, Mr. Ruez.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then again on Banja Luka television on 24th January 1996, questioned as to the acts, Radovan Karadzic said: "Our Army did not commit war crimes. Our Army followed orders from the General Staff and the General Staff Commander. Therefore, our Army and our police did not commit crimes".

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Would you read the next sentence as well, just continue with that one sentence more?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "The propaganda against us will turn to our advantage one day".

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: OK. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 12th February 1996, in the course of an interview with The Times Radovan Karadzic said: "In connection with these so-called massacres of Muslims in Srebrenica, there was no order to kill them. Nobody under my command would dare kill those who were arrested or captured as prisoners of war. I am absolutely fully involved. Everything concerning the Serb Republic is in my hands". Amongst other reactions on the part of Radovan Karadzic is the promotion of General Krsic and Zivanovic who are the masterminds of the Serb victory over Srebrenica, so they got a promotion as a result of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Ruez. Your Honours, that concludes our presentation.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harmon. Now we will move on to questions. Let me first turn to Judge Riad, whether you have any questions, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, first, I would like to thank you for having spoken so clearly and for giving us all these details. That said, I would like you to confirm some of the conclusions we are likely to draw. First, I deduce from what you said that deportation, detention etc., transport for execution operations took place quickly, very carefully and on a very large scale to the point that in the course of a single day there were 25,000 people evacuated. That was on 13th July. You being an expert, was that feasible without a lot of co-ordination in terms of logistics and without having his high command that would be co-ordinating the whole process? To take it a step further, would it be feasible without the assent of the supreme commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes, on 12th July, there was a first group of about 5,000 persons that was evacuated. Then on 13th July, the remainder of the refugee population at Potocari was evacuated. So that was 20,000. So 25,000 people over two days. In fact, things went ahead quicker than planned by General Mladic, because the military observers there said that he was even surprised to have done with the whole operation by the 13th. Apparently, the 14th had also been scheduled with finishing up that operation. So the observers they were also struck by the large number of buses that were there, a large number of trucks as well. It is quite clear that the preparation of the evacuation had been carried out in quite some detail. The civil transport companies had certainly been commandeered for that purpose, and it was local companies who provided the vehicles -- mining companies and transport companies, in fact.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: So there was a certain amount of co-operation on the part of several administrations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes. All this equipment had to be made available in advance.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: (No translation of the question)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Given the efficiency with which everything unfolded, there is no doubt that there was a pre-established plan for that deportation.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You said that when he entered Srebrenica, General Mladic indicated, I do not remember exactly what the words he used were, that "Finally, we have revenged the 1804 uprising against the Turks", that was before the massacres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: That was when he entered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is when he entered Srebrenica on 11th July.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: So was he calling on people to seek revenge or what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it is not really for me to comment on that. All I can do is deal with that statement with the historical reference.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What exactly did it say? Let me get hold of it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Srebrenica is now Serbian on 11th July 1995. The evening of another great Serbian festival we offer the city to the Serbian people. After the rebellion against the Dahijas, the moment has now arrived to avenge ourselves of the Turks in this region".

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: "To avenge ourselves"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, "The time has come to avenge ourselves of the Turks in this region". This is the translation of the comment that I have of Mladic's comments that day.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Afterwards, General Mladic, according to the latest information you have, he was present five times you were able to give details about, in Srebrenica, in Potocari, Bratunac, at the prisoners (sic) field and in the school and in the execution site right before the execution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The execution had already been begun.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: He is the one who was speaking to the detainees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he systematically spoke to the detainees every time came to a site.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: So that one could say that he directed the operations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can only say that he was speaking to them. He was after all the commander of the army.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: He was present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was present.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: His presence has been established. However, what do you have to say about Dr. Karadzic's participation? Was he present at any time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Radovan Karadzic was never seen at the sites when the acts took place, which is why the only reference we have to him are the declaration that he himself made to the press.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: As when he said that "everything is in my hands", that is when he assumed the principal role?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the comment that he made to the press that day, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: In respect of the Dutch Battalion, there was a statement from Mladic. He said that he was threatening to kill the hostages, the 55 hostages. How were these hostages taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that Colonel Karremans would be in a better position to speak to you about that. The investigation for which I am responsible starts with the enclave and mainly is focused on the fate of the prisoners. The military operational aspect prior to the fall of the enclave was not the purpose of our investigation, but I am sure that the Colonel will address that issue at the proper time.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Therefore, you do not know how they were able table to take that truck which had the clothes of the United Nations people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the equipment which was stolen from the Dutch blue helmets was done by force. It was either through using weapons or using the fact that there was no way that they would be able to oppose the desire of the Bosnian Serb soldiers surrounding them, and they would have to give over the equipment that was being asked.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ODIO BENITO
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ruez, do you know how many people there were in Srebrenica from the beginning of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to the estimates which have been given, at the beginning of the operation which led to the fall of the enclave, the population of that was about 40,000 in addition to a certain number of military personnel. The number of that personnel, however, is not known. The estimates concerning the number of military personnel fluctuate between 3,000 and 6,000.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Were they all ordinarily from Srebrenica or where they displaced civilians, refugees, coming from other safe areas like Zepa, Gorazde, Bihac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. The population which comprised the enclave of July 1995 came from the Srebrenica region, but also from those surrounding regions where the ethnic cleansing was going on and chasing out people, especially from Zvornik and from Vlasenica, in the direction of the enclave. That municipality actually had been brought into a single unit at the time the enclave was taken. The entire Muslim population of the area which could no longer cross the current separation zone, that is, the old frontline, took refuge in that enclave, and the enclaves communicate among one another, that is, Zepa and Srebrenica when it came to supplies and anything having to do with the black market.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Yes, because, according to the Security Council resolutions from 1993, the ethnic cleansing had begun in 1993 in this region. So I suppose there were a lot of refugees and displaced persons around this area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. The population of Srebrenica under ordinary conditions was about 7,000. Therefore, it had swollen up to 40,000 in July of 1995. Before that situation in 1993 already, the population had swollen very significantly and a part of that population was able to get back to Muslim territory after intervention by UNPROFOR which took place at the beginning of 1993, that is, in March.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: In this connection, do you know if these displaced people were basically sick and wounded people, women, children and elderly people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they were all types of cases. Among the many witnesses that we spoke with, many came from places where they had lost everything because of the fighting. Their physical condition was no worse than anywhere else, except for the fact that the enclave itself had problems having to do with supplies. But the population was divided, distributed normally. There were families, there were children.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Yes, but among these displaced people, were there sick, wounded, elderly, women, children and families, of course, but .....

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, yes of course. Those people who were evacuated from the enclave, all of them who arrived -- actually we did not see part of the video which was prepared on that subject. We can see families with women and children arriving, and already by the end of June 1995 all the women and children were in Tuzla, and most of them on the air base where there were 6,000 people. They were put into various centres in Tuzla and around Tuzla, but the people, those who were not there were the men. The elderly could be evacuated, and the medical convoys ran into many problems which probably would be too long to go into details about here, but in general most of the wounded later on were exchanged, but they were just about the only ones who were able to be exchanged and the release of prisoners which took place at the beginning of the year affected a very small number of people who came from the Srebrenica enclave when one compares them to the number of people that are missing.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: For the Tribunal's record, it is obvious that there were large numbers of women arriving in Potocari. Do you mean how many, approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you describe what happened to those women in and around Potocari, basically in those factories that night, that terrible night, after the fall of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were the victims of the same type of crimes as the other people there. There were not specifically targeted at that point. Those who were targeted were the men. The Bosnian Serb soldiers were more interested in the male population of the enclave. The women were affected indirectly but were not actually targeted during the operation. The apparent objective of the Potocari situation was to allow the crimes to be committed in a public enough way, so that the population on site would be terrorized and then to evacuate the site as quickly as possible. In fact, this is the situation -- is Mladic's main argument which puts forth two points, that is, that everything that was done was done at the request of the civilian representatives of the population. We spoke about what had to do with those representatives. The second point is that the departure of those populations was a voluntary one; that everything was done to make this voluntary departure into something which was organised.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What you are basically saying is that the horror on the hill was the same for everybody there. Do you know whether or not there were Bosnian Serb paramilitary units taking part in the operation that followed the fall of Srebrenica or only regular troops?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is information according to which there was paramilitary involvement in that. The investigation which is now going on into the perpetrators is continuing, so the identification of those who participated in the military operation, on the one hand, and in the exterminating operation, on the other, is still going on and for the time being it is difficult to give any specific facts about this since it is still under review.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ODIO BENITO
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, this is a beginning question. What is the status of the enclave, according to the Security Council resolutions, what type of protection was it supposed to offer, quickly? I think that for the records of the Trial Chamber it would be important to have specifics on that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can rely on what the Prosecutor tells me about this, but since this investigation has taken a lot of time, I did not look at all into the question of the legal status.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: No, I am not looking for a legal status; simply, what was the level of protection that the international community gave to those enclaves? How many enclaves were there? What was the status of those who were taking refuge? I can then turn to you, Mr. Harmon, for that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do not think Mr. Ruez is the person to answer that specifically with the enclave in Srebrenica. Our next witness, Colonel Karremans, will be testifying about the enclave and the level of protection in the enclave.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The other question that I wanted to ask you, Mr. Ruez, is whether, in your opinion, could you tell us why Srebrenica was chosen and why so late, when we look at the chronology of events? Since July 1995 the conflict has been going on for several years; the international community is aware of what is going on; I might even dare say that our Tribunal has already been created. Why Srebrenica? Why at that specific time? Was there an historical, a strategic, a cultural or a media interest? Do you have any opinion you would like to put forth about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have an opinion, but it is a personal one and is not specifically related to the investigation. The only thing that I could really state, but will be a personal opinion -- I am not an expert in the matter -- so the only thing that I can say having to do with those acts that were committed, that is, having to do with historical context or the reasons for it were not the purpose of the investigation.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Turning again to Mr. Harmon, would you like to supplement anything that was given as a partial answer to that question?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Not at the moment, your Honour. I would be prepared to address that in my remarks at the end of the presentation.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: All right. I would like to ask you a question having to do with the statement from Radovan Karadzic that you quoted from The Times. This is a question I can either ask you or the Prosecutor. Do you consider these being completely in support of General Mladic or do you have the feeling that there was some slight difference between their points of view, some specific, distinct separation specifically in the declaration which appeared in The Times where he said that those soldiers finally obeyed an order? I do not know which of you would like to answer this question, whether this is a personal opinion or whether the Prosecutor would prefer to answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Again, your Honour, I am prepared to answer that question, if the court pleases, at the end of my summation to your Honours. Mr. Ruez is a fact witness here to describe the facts of his investigation and his particular findings and is not in a position to give opinions such as the ones the court has asked. I will be prepared to answer those questions for you, your Honour, at a later time.
